subject: On‑prem DNS assertion + egress TLS bridge (airgapped tenant) — architecture review
messages:
From: Paul Carlson <pcarlson@fintechcorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeOps Solutions <ops@edgeops.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem DNS assertion + egress TLS bridge (airgapped tenant) — initial ask

Hey Jordan,

We're getting into the design phase for a private deployment of Redwood in one of our regional data centers (air‑gapped vlan). Two questions that are blocking procurement/security signoff:

1) How does Redwood recommend asserting private DNS for tenant FQDNs when the tenant does not want us to host any authoritative zones? They want their internal resolver to stay authoritative and only allow our service to be reachable via a controlled egress/bridge.

2) For TLS termination: they want inbound client connections to validate server certs but prefer the TLS termination to occur at an egress bridge we operate in their VPC, with client auth (mTLS) between that bridge and Redwood’s internal runtime. Keys: who hosts certs, how rotation/OCSP will work, and what proof of possession the tenant needs to provide for CSR acceptance.

I attached a rough network sketch (fintechcorp-network-sketch.pdf). Can we schedule a short architecture review this week? Security wants a written runbook for the pattern they can attach to the SOC audit.

Thanks,
Paul Carlson
Director, Platform Architecture
FinTechCorp

P.S. EdgeOps is included—Matt from EdgeOps will help with the egress bridge implementation.
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Paul Carlson <pcarlson@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>, EdgeOps Solutions <ops@edgeops.com>

Subject: Re: On‑prem DNS assertion + egress TLS bridge (airgapped tenant) — initial ask

Paul — thanks for the clear summary and the sketch, that helps a lot. High level we support two proven patterns depending on customer requirements:

- Pattern A (split‑horizon stub): Customer keeps authoritative zone and configures a stub / forwarder for the tenant FQDNs toward a resolver we host in the egress bridge. We never host the zone; customer retains control. Works well when the tenant allows outbound DNS to a managed resolver.

- Pattern B (assertion + proxy): Customer keeps authority but provides signed assertions (CSR + proof of possession) that we map to internal hostnames in our private runtime. DNS remains with customer; we rely on the egress bridge to present an internal alias and proxy TLS to Redwood. This is the recommended path when strict zone ownership is required and cross‑site DNS is restricted.

For TLS/certs: we typically recommend the tenant manage leaf certs for client‑facing gateways (they keep their private keys if required). Where customers allow, we can host the bridge TLS cert (with delegated CSR flow) and run mutual TLS between the bridge and Redwood (our side uses customer‑bound certs). Rotation options: short‑lived leaf certs + automated CSR renewal via ACME over preprovisioned tunnel, or static PKI with Rollover window and signed rotation events. OCSP stapling will be supported by the bridge if it has outbound access to the tenant's OCSP responder or a public CA.

I want to triage a few specific items before the call so we can provide a runbook:
- Does FinTechCorp allow egress DNS to a managed IP in their VPC? (stub vs full forwarder)
- Are they comfortable with us hosting the bridge certificate (we can offer HSM backed keys under Dedicated contract) or do they insist on customer‑owned keys?
- Expected connection topology: VPN backhaul, private peer, or direct internet NAT from the bridge?

Marissa and Mina — looping you in for cert lifecycle and runtime routing input. Paul — propose Thu 09/16 10:00–10:30 PT for an architecture call; if that works I’ll calendar‑invite and share a short agenda.

—Jordan

Jordan Blake

Subject: Re: On‑prem DNS assertion + egress TLS bridge (airgapped tenant) — initial ask

Jordan / team — quick internal notes I drafted after reviewing the sketch and Jordan’s options. Posting here so FinTechCorp has visibility.

Option 1 — Stub/Forward to Redwood Resolver (lower operational complexity):
- Customer keeps authoritative zones. They configure a forwarder or stub zone in their resolver for tenant.* pointing at the bridge resolver IP(s).
- Pros: minimal chain of custody for DNS, tenant retains full control of records.
- Cons: requires outbound DNS from tenant to the bridge; some air‑gapped sites block this.

Option 2 — Assertion + Proxy (recommended for strict custody):
- Customer signs CSRs or issues a signed assertion (JWT + proof of possession) mapping their FQDNs to a token we register. The egress bridge does not answer public DNS — it only proxies TLS and rewrites SNI to the internal runtime name.
- Pros: tenant authoritative, no zone hosting by Redwood; supports air‑gapped setups where DNS egress is restricted.
- Cons: additional onboarding to establish assertion workflow; more complex rotation and audit trails.

For the certificate lifecycle and trust:
- If customer wants to keep private keys, we validate CSR signatures and require a short‑lived attestation token (signed by tenant KMS). Renewal: automated pull model (bridge fetches new CSR via mutually authenticated channel) or push model (tenant posts new signed CSR to our ingestion endpoint).
- OCSP: recommend stapling at the bridge. If the tenant’s CA is internal, the bridge must be able to reach the internal OCSP responder or the tenant must provide revocation metadata in the assertion.
- Audit/logs: we will provide signed rotation events and an access log (hashes of certs) suitable for SOC artifacts.

Operational ask for call: please have the customer's DNS policy (allow/deny outbound DNS), CA provisioning policy (can they sign CSRs for third parties), and network topology (VPN / private peer / NAT) on hand.

—M.

Marissa Cole
Senior Product Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: On‑prem DNS assertion + egress TLS bridge (airgapped tenant) — initial ask

Jordan / Marissa / Mina — thanks for the rapid breakdown. We discussed internally and the customer is leaning toward Option 2 (Assertion + Proxy) — they will not permit outbound DNS to external resolvers. They are OK with the bridge being run by EdgeOps in their VPC, and they prefer Redwood to hold the bridge certificate under HSM if we can provide the required audit trail and an automated rotation schedule.

Questions before the call:
- Rotation windows: what default lifetime do you recommend for bridge certs? We prefer short lived but need alignment with our internal CA policy.
- Can OCSP stapling be performed if the CA is internal and unreachable from the bridge? If not, can the assertion include revocation metadata as you suggested?
- For the CSR/proof flow: we can sign a short attestation token with our KMS. Will Redwood accept an ACME‑like REST CSR exchange over the tunnel, or do you need a different API?

I attached a short draft MOU (redwood-mtap-proposal-v1.docx) describing the roles — it’s rough but should help scope the runbook. Thu 10/16 10:00 PT still works for us if you can confirm the calendar invite.

—Paul
